name: webpack-externals-does-not-block-analysis
hook: webpack externals doesn't prevent analysis of node: scheme imports
body: webpack.externals marks a module as external so it's not emitted in the bundle, but webpack still analyzes the module for tree-shaking. When analyzing undici (marked external), webpack follows internal imports and encounters 'node:console' / 'node:crypto' etc. which fail because no webpack plugin handles the node: protocol. The fix is to ALSO add resolve.alias to redirect node: imports to an empty stub.
why: CI failed with 'UnhandledSchemeError: Reading from node:console is not handled by plugins' even after adding undici to webpack.externals. The externals approach alone was insufficient because webpack still analyzes the module internals.

name: next-config-js-uses-esm-require-unavailable
hook: next.config.js is ESM — use path.resolve not require.resolve
body: next.config.js uses ESM (import at top level), so require is not available. When adding webpack resolve.alias entries that need a file path, use path.resolve(process.cwd(), ...) instead of require.resolve(...). process.cwd() gives the project root at build time, matching what require.resolve would have resolved to.
why: CI failed with 'ReferenceError: require is not defined' at next.config.js:155 because the file is ESM but used require.resolve in the webpack config callback.

name: externalize-metapackage-also-externalize-platform-packages
hook: Externalizing a metapackage requires regex pattern to catch resolved platform-specific packages
body: When a metapackage like @napi-rs/canvas resolves to platform-specific packages (@napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-gnu, @napi-rs/canvas-darwin-x64, etc.), simply adding the metapackage name to webpack externals is insufficient. Webpack resolves the platform-specific name and those packages are not in externals. Use a regex external pattern like /^@napi-rs\/canvas-/ to catch all platform variants.
why: CI failed with 'Node.js binary module ...skia.linux-x64-gnu.node is not supported in the browser' because @napi-rs/canvas was externalized but @napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-gnu was not, even though the former is just a metapackage that resolves to the latter.

name: webpack-resolve-alias-does-not-support-regex
hook: webpack 5 resolve.alias does not support regex — use resolve.fallback for node: protocol
body: webpack 5's resolve.alias does NOT support regex string patterns. A key like '^node:(.*)$' is treated as a literal string, not a regex. The correct webpack 5 API for redirecting Node.js built-in modules (node:console, node:crypto, node:dns, etc.) is resolve.fallback with { node: false }. Setting node: false tells webpack these modules are unavailable (returns empty object), which satisfies the resolver for all node: scheme imports at once.
why: CI still failed with 'UnhandledSchemeError: Reading from node:console' after adding the regex alias in resolve.alias — the regex was treated as a literal key and never matched, so node: imports were still unresolved.
